baseline.goal: A work turn counts as running until the server's stream closes. While it runs, the screen shows what is running (including the gate after the answer), a live clock that survives a reattach, and the actual Bash command. A note written meanwhile waits and is sent when the turn ends. Clicking a quoted source opens it even when it is a hub page or a bare file name.
out: How long the gate takes or what it runs (`python -m pytest tool` stays as it is)
The server's single-turn hold per worktree and its 409 for a second sender (another window can still get it)
How the answer itself quotes sources (fixed on the reading side, not by changing prompts)
done: In `web/src/lib/work.ts`, a `done` event no longer ends the turn: `pending` stays true and the reattach logic still treats the turn as unfinished until the stream closes. Steps that arrive after `done` (the gate's notes from `specs.check`) show under the answer in the same turn.

Every event `Run.put` emits carries a server timestamp `ts` (epoch seconds), for Claude and Codex turns alike, and `/api/work/events` replays it. A test in `tool/test_main.py` (or the work tests) asserts `ts` is present and does not decrease across a turn's events, including the gate's notes.

The latest step of a running turn shows `⟳ 실행 중 · m분 s초`, counted from that step's server `ts`. It shows `답을 기다린다` while an approval is open and `마무리 중` after the answer has arrived. The labels are the same for Claude and Codex turns. After a page reload mid-turn the clock continues from the server time, not from 0.

An instruction sent while the turn is still running (including after its answer) is shown as `대기 · 이 턴이 끝나면 보낸다`, can be cancelled, and is sent as the next turn once the stream closes. Sending this way gets no 409.

A Claude Bash tool line shows both description and command, e.g. `Bash · Run the tests · $ python -m pytest -q tool`. Other tools keep their current one-line summary. A unit test covers `_tool_brief` for Bash with and without `description`.

`/api/file` resolves in order: the path in the checkout → a hub page (`craft/…`, `operator/…`, `.md` optional) under the wiki root → the one file in the checkout whose path ends with the given name. If several match, it picks the most recently touched: uncommitted changes first (by mtime), then by last commit time. If they are still tied, it returns the candidates and the screen lists them as clickable choices. It never serves anything outside the checkout or the wiki root. Tests in `tool/test_main.py` cover each branch, including the tie and the outside-root refusal.
Every `path[:line]` citation in the existing answer records that used to fail is replayed against the new `/api/file`. All of them open, and any that do not are listed by name in the PR.

Observed in the app window on a real running turn: the gate step appears under the answer with a running clock, a reload keeps the clock going, a note written after the answer shows as waiting and goes out as the next turn when the gate finishes, and a Bash line shows `$ command`. If the session cannot drive the window itself, it stops before the done report and asks the person to confirm this.

decisions.what: The end of a turn is the close of the server's stream, not the `done` event
decisions.why: `run_turn` keeps holding the worktree through `specs.check` (the ~6 min gate) after `done`, and releases before `run.finish()`. So the stream close is the first moment a new turn will not hit 409.
decisions.rejected: Moving the gate off the turn's hold onto a separate job: it would let another write land while the gate runs, which the hold exists to prevent

decisions.what: The server stamps `ts` in `Run.put`. The screen corrects for clock skew once per stream (receipt time vs. first event `ts`) and counts the clock from the latest step's `ts`.
decisions.why: One place covers both hosts and the gate notes. Server time makes a reattached screen continue the clock instead of restarting it.
decisions.rejected: Timing on the client from when it saw the event: a reload would reset the clock to 0

decisions.what: Instructions written during a running turn are queued per worktree, in order, each cancellable, and sent one by one after each stream closes
decisions.why: Settled without the person: an ordered queue keeps every note and never sends two into one hold
decisions.rejected: Keeping only the last note (silently drops earlier ones) or steering it into the running turn (after the answer the agent is no longer listening)

decisions.what: The Bash brief appends `$ <command>` after the description, keeping the existing collapsed-whitespace truncation
decisions.why: `_tool_brief` stops at the first key, so `description` hid the command entirely
decisions.rejected: Showing only the command: the description is what the person reads first

decisions.what: `/api/file` falls back checkout → hub page → unique name suffix. Ties are broken by recency (uncommitted mtime, then last commit), and a remaining tie returns candidates as data in a 200 reply rather than an error.
decisions.why: Answers quote hub pages and bare names (`7-verify.md`, `Query.tsx`). The recently touched file is almost always the one meant. When it is not decidable, listing candidates beats a wrong file.
decisions.rejected: Returning the first match: it silently opens the wrong file when names repeat

fix: 도는 작업이 보이게 — 게이트까지 턴으로, 실행 중 시계, 실제 명령어, 출처 찾기

## 무엇이 문제였나

- **P0 — 멈춘 건지 모른다.** 에이전트가 답한 뒤에도 서버는 작업트리를 쥔 채 명세 게이트(`python -m pytest tool`, 약 6분)를 돌린다. 화면은 답에서 턴을 끝냈기 때문에, 그동안 적은 다음 지시가 새 턴으로 나가 409 "이 작업트리의 에이전트가 아직 돌고 있다" 를 받았다. 무엇이 도는지는 화면 어디에도 없었다.
- 출처를 누르면 "그 파일이 없다" 가 자주 떴다. 답이 허브 문서(`craft/…`, `operator/…`)나 파일 이름만(`7-verify.md`, `Query.tsx`) 인용하기 때문이다.

## 바꾼 것

- 턴은 서버의 실행이 끝날 때(스트림이 닫힐 때)까지 도는 것으로 본다. 답 뒤에 온 단계(게이트)는 답 아래에 선다.
- 가장 최근 단계에 "⟳ 실행 중 · m분 s초". 모든 턴 이벤트에 서버 시각 `ts` 를 실어, 다시 붙어도 시계가 이어진다. 열린 승인은 "답을 기다린다", 답 뒤에는 "마무리 중". 두 호스트가 같다.
- 답 뒤에 적은 지시는 "대기 · 이 턴이 끝나면 보낸다" 로 두었다가 끝나면 다음 턴으로 보낸다(취소 가능).
- Claude 도구 줄에 설명 옆 실제 명령어: `Bash · Run the tests · $ python -m pytest -q tool`.
- `/api/file`: 체크아웃 기준 → 허브 문서 → 그 이름으로 끝나는 파일 하나. 여럿이면 가장 최근에 손댄 것(커밋 안 된 것, 그다음 커밋 순), 그래도 같으면 후보를 알려 준다. 기록의 실패 인용을 모두 다시 돌려 전부 열리는 것을 확인했다.

## 확인

- `python -m pytest -q tool` — 490 passed (이후 `tool/test_main.py` 51 passed 재확인)
- `npm run build` 통과
- 창에서 실제 도는 턴으로 보는 확인은 아직
